correctness.rationale: For 1/sqrt2<=R<=1, interior of a unit lattice square is covered only by its four corners. Thus the unoccupied fraction equals integral q^{k_R(x)} and is a finite polynomial; a surviving disk contributes an exposed arc exactly when all m_R(theta) other disks covering its boundary fail, giving a second finite polynomial. At R=1, adjacent two-deletion corners leave area c=1-sqrt(3)/4-pi/6 and arc length pi/3 per pattern; three deletions leave 1-pi/4 area and pi/2 arc. The coefficients give Phi_1=4cq²(1-q)²+4(1-pi/4)q³(1-q)+q⁴, Lambda_1=(4pi/3)q²(1-q)²+2pi q³(1-q). The near-critical isolated deleted-site cavity has diameter ~2delta in both axes, area 4delta² and perimeter 8delta; two-failure coefficients tend to 4c and 4pi/3 by dominated convergence. Uniform bounded higher polynomial coefficients prove both windows; the lattice ergodic theorem supplies almost-sure density limits. Independent midpoint integration of quarter cavity gives area/delta² =4.0135708 at delta=.01, 4.0026760 at .002, and 4.0006701 at .0005. The earlier scratch integration with reversed limits was discarded and corrected before accepting this check.

value.rationale: A sharp distinction between two natural geometric coverage-loss observables on the standard square sensor grid, with exact all-q critical laws and separate reliability scales q~(1-R)² versus q~1-R. Boundary length and area encode different geometry and matter for quantitative reliability; this is neither a mere coverage/no-coverage criterion nor a triangular-grid substitution.
